context_notes: The PR metadata incorrectly claims 2 files in 'internal/auth' and 'internal/payments'. The actual changes span 7 files across 'internal/config', 'internal/node', and 'internal/reasoners'. All changes relate to three coherent themes: (1) consolidating OpenAI-compatible provider configuration for the opencode harness, (2) enforcing strict key+base URL pairing for the direct AI path, and (3) changing meta-selector parse failures from fail-open (seeded confidence 0.7) to fail-closed (return error).
pr_narrative: This PR consolidates the OpenAI-compatible AI provider configuration used by both the opencode harness subprocess and the direct `.ai()` Go SDK path. Previously the harness used a catch-all environment-variable forwarding (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, etc.), while the direct path used OpenRouter-specific model ID parsing with a `openrouter/` prefix strip. The new mechanism unifies both paths on a single contract: `OPENAI_API_KEY` + `OPENAI_BASE_URL` must be provided together; if only one is set, `BuildAgent` rejects the configuration at boot. For the opencode harness specifically, instead of forwarding raw credentials, it now writes a JSON config blob (`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`) containing a 'compat' OpenCode provider definition with the model, base URL, API key, and an npm package reference. The model ID is normalized: `openai/<model>` becomes `compat/<model>` in the harness config while retaining the full `openai/<model>` as the runtime model. The `openrouter/` prefix strip logic is preserved for backward compatibility with existing OpenRouter deployments. In the meta-selector reasoner, error handling around harness structured output is hardened: a nil or error-result from the harness no longer produces a seeded fallback (lens + 0.7 confidence + empty dimensions) but instead propagates a descriptive error indicating which model failed and why.
risk_surfaces: node/node.go:176-180 — `BuildAgent` now rejects if OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_BASE_URL is set but not both. Any caller passing only one of these two env vars will receive an error where previously it may have silently ignored the partial config or used OpenRouter as fallback. This is a breaking change for any integration relying on the old partial-config behavior.

node/node.go:196-200 — The `aiModelForAPI` function now strips BOTH `openrouter/` and `openai/` prefixes. Previously only `openrouter/` was stripped. If any caller uses an `openai/` prefixed model ID for non-opencode providers, that prefix will now be incorrectly removed, changing the effective model sent to the upstream API.

config/ai.go:79-101 — `ProviderEnv()` now diverges behavior by provider: for `opencode` it no longer forwards `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY` even if they are set. These are silently dropped for opencode. Any deployment relying on these keys being forwarded to opencode (e.g., using a multi-provider fallback within opencode) will break silently.

config/ai.go:109-142 — `HarnessRuntimeModel()` and `opencodeConfigContent()` are new methods. If `c.Provider != "opencode"` but `c.HarnessModel` contains `openai/`, these methods will still execute their prefix-stripping logic, potentially producing unexpected model names in the harness config. The logic assumes `openai/` prefix only appears for the opencode provider.

reasoners/meta.go:55-68 — `runMetaLens` now returns an error on nil/errored harness results instead of a seeded fallback. Any caller of `MetaSemantic` or `MetaQuality` expecting a fallback result (with lens, 0.7 confidence, empty dimensions) on harness failure will instead receive an error. This changes the contract of meta-selector results.

reasoners/contexts_test.go:128-130 and reasoners_test.go:394-405 — The meta-selector test expectations flipped from expecting success-with-fallback to expecting error. If any production code path relied on the old fail-open behavior (which the tests explicitly documented as matching Python's behavior), those paths will now error instead of proceeding with seeded values.

config/ai.go:79 — When `c.Provider == "opencode"` but `openAIKey` or `openAIBase` is empty, the code falls through to the legacy `else` branch that forwards all env vars. This means opencode with missing credentials gets the old behavior. This dual-path behavior may not be intentional and could mask configuration errors.

node/node_test.go:146-158 — New test `TestBuildAgentPartialOpenAIConfigRejected` validates the strict pairing requirement. This test sets `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=legacy-dummy` alongside partial OpenAI config and expects rejection. If a deployment has both legacy OpenRouter and partial OpenAI env vars set, the new code will reject the startup. Previously it would have used OpenRouter.
intent_gaps: The PR metadata says 'Local Diff Review' with clusters for 'internal/auth' and 'internal/payments' — these directories do not exist in the actual diff. The metadata appears to be a template artifact and does not reflect the actual changed files.

The diff introduces `HarnessRuntimeModel()` and `opencodeConfigContent()` methods on `AIIntegrationConfig` that generate a JSON config blob with an npm package (`opencode-npm-pr-af-openai-compat`). The origin and purpose of this npm package name is not explained in comments or PR description. Reviewers cannot assess whether this package is safe, maintained, or intended for this use case.

The `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` JSON includes a `small_model` field set to the same value as `model`. This doubles the model entry. There is no explanation of why `small_model` is needed or what runtime behavior it controls.

The PR changes meta-selector behavior from fail-open to fail-closed. The original seeded fallback (lens + 0.7 confidence + empty dimensions + empty rationale) was explicitly documented in tests as matching Python behavior. The PR provides no rationale for abandoning this contract. A reviewer should ask why the fail-open behavior was removed.

The change to `aiModelForAPI` now strips `openai/` prefix in addition to `openrouter/`. The old comment described stripping `openrouter/` as necessary because 'LiteLLM consumes the prefix'. The new comment says 'provider prefixes are routing metadata and must not be sent'. These are different justifications for the same operation. The `openai/` stripping is new and unexplained.

No migration path is documented for existing deployments using OPENROUTER_API_KEY with the opencode provider. Those deployments will no longer have their key forwarded to opencode, and opencode will use the new JSON config instead. This is likely intentional but undocumented.
unrelated_changes: The change to `reasoners/contexts_test.go:125-128` flipping the expected error direction appears semantically unrelated to the OpenAI-compatible provider consolidation. It is a test-expectation change driven by a behavioral change in `reasoners/meta.go`, but the behavioral change (fail-open to fail-closed) is tangentially related to the provider config changes only insofar as both touch the harness. This is a bundled secondary change that should be reviewed separately.

The change to `reasoners/reasoners_test.go:386-405` renaming test comments and flipping expectations from 'seeded 0.7 fallback' to 'fail closed' is a test-only change driven by the same meta-selector behavioral change. It belongs with the meta-selector changes, not the config normalization.
